channel.title: Updated · all tabs
channel.description: Daily news and research, explained: every tab

item.title: F5 issues emergency hotfixes for critical BIG-IP flaws that can crash traffic handling and may allow remote code execution
item.description: F5 released out-of-band hotfixes for critical, unauthenticated BIG-IP flaws that can crash its traffic engine and may allow remote code execution; no mitigations exist besides patching. (BleepingComputer, Canadian Centre for Cyber Security)

item.title: Amazon says suspected Chinese hackers used the AI agent framework Cairn to find and exploit a zero-day at East Asian universities
item.description: Amazon found an exposed Cairn server showing AI agents that worked for hours without human direction, then discovered and used an unknown flaw in a medical imaging app to take over university servers. (The Record, The Register)

item.title: UK surveillance tribunal confirms the Home Office served Apple a secret order over encrypted iCloud data
item.description: The Investigatory Powers Tribunal rejected the Home Office's secrecy argument and confirmed it served Apple a Technical Capability Notice, though the order's content stays secret ahead of a 2027 hearing. (Investigatory Powers Tribunal judgment, The Register)

item.title: Signal blocks screenshots by default to keep Siri and Gemini agents from reading private chats
item.description: Signal's iOS and Android apps now block screenshots by default so built-in AI agents cannot capture chats, and the company says operating systems give developers no robust way to stop such access. (The Register, Engadget)

item.title: Polymorph: Operating System Kernel Optimization Through Artificial Intelligence
item.description: Polymorph has an AI agent write one tunable Linux kernel policy, then tunes it live without a language model, beating Linux's defaults for page caching and scheduling at far lower cost than offline search. (Dean Sysman, Georgios Liargkovas, Tal Zussman et al.)

item.title: A daily KRAS-blocking pill plus chemotherapy stops tumour growth in 90% of patients with advanced pancreatic cancer in an early trial
item.description: In a 61-patient phase 1/2 trial, daraxonrasib plus standard chemotherapy shrank tumours in just over 60% of people newly diagnosed with metastatic pancreatic cancer; 76.6% were alive at one year. (BBC News, The Guardian)

item.title: FDA grants accelerated approval to GSK's Nelkarmi for ALK-positive lung cancer that has outgrown earlier drugs
item.description: The FDA cleared neladalkib, a daily pill, for advanced ALK-positive non-small cell lung cancer after earlier ALK inhibitors stop working, based on response rates of 49% and 32% in a 222-patient trial. (pharmaphorum, chemXplore)

item.title: Retatrutide Once Weekly in Adults with Knee Osteoarthritis Pain and Obesity
item.description: In two phase 3 trials with 1,019 adults with obesity and painful knee osteoarthritis, weekly retatrutide injections cut pain scores and body weight significantly more than placebo, with more serious side effects. (Thomas J. Schnitzer David J. Hunter Philip G. Conaghan Arya M. Sharma Sue D. Pedersen Kaiyi Chen So Young Park Nune Makarova Kathryn Giblin and Tammy Forresterthe TRIUMPH-4 and TRIUMPH-1-OA Investigators* · Northwestern University Feinberg School of Medicine; University of Sydney; University of Leeds; University of Alberta; University of Calgary; Eli Lilly and Company)

item.title: A DNA Typewriter records the cell lineage history of a mouse, from zygote to late organogenesis
item.description: A DNA recorder inserted into a fertilized mouse egg wrote an ordered log of cell divisions into the genome, letting researchers rebuild a mouse embryo's cell family tree from the first division to organ formation. (Qi Yu, Haedong Kim, Sophie Seidel et al. · University of Washington School of Medicine; Howard Hughes Medical Institute; Dartmouth College)

item.title: Spatial transcriptomics reveals molecular organization of human and nonhuman primate basal ganglia
item.description: Mapping where each cell type sits in the basal ganglia of humans, macaques and marmosets, researchers found a highly stereotyped layout shared across primates and often with mice, with gene gradients laid over discrete compartments. (Madeleine N. Hewitt, Meghan A. Turner, Nelson Johansen et al. · Allen Institute for Brain Science; Princeton Neuroscience Institute; Leiden University Medical Center; Delft University of Technology; The Rockefeller University; Massachusetts Institute of Technology; Washington University in St. Louis; RIKEN; Kyoto University; University of Washington)

item.title: BepiColombo reaches Mercury after an eight-year voyage and prepares to become the second spacecraft ever to orbit it
item.description: The European-Japanese BepiColombo mission has arrived at Mercury after more than eight years and is set to fire its thrusters to enter orbit, with science operations due to begin in April. (The Guardian, BBC News)

item.title: The US sells its first deep-sea mining leases, off American Samoa, to a single bidder days after a court faulted the review
item.description: The Interior Department sold two seabed lease areas covering 31.5 million acres off American Samoa for the $6 million minimum, with one company bidding, three days after a judge found the wildlife review unlawful. (gCaptain, Yahoo News (AFP), Nature World News)

item.title: Physicists send a "practically unblockable" message through a brick wall by moving an elevator's counterweight and measuring its gravity
item.description: University of Queensland physicists encoded the word "gravity" in the position of a 1.8-tonne elevator counterweight and read it through a wall with a gravimeter, at one bit per minute. (University of Queensland via EurekAlert!, The Guardian)

item.title: Quantum position verification with remote untrusted devices
item.description: Using entangled photons and a loophole-free Bell test across a 195-metre network, NIST-led researchers certified that a remote party really sat in a target region, without trusting its hardware. (Gautam A. Kavuri, Yanbao Zhang, Abigail R. Gookin et al. · National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST))

item.title: Quantum-classical separation in bounded-resource tasks arising from measurement contextuality
item.description: On a superconducting quantum processor, Google researchers used contextuality to win cooperative games and solve a structured problem at success rates no classical strategy can reach. (Google Quantum AI and CollaboratorsS. Kumar, E. Rosenberg, A. Grajales Dau et al. · Google Quantum AI)

item.title: US retail sales rise just 0.2% in October as car purchases fall and prices outpace spending
item.description: US retail and food-service sales rose 0.2% in October to $748.2 billion, slowing from 0.8% in September, as auto dealers' sales fell and consumer prices rose faster than spending. (U.S. Census Bureau, StockAnalysis, The Globe and Mail)

item.title: Walmart raises its annual outlook for the third time as US online sales grow 23%
item.description: Walmart's quarterly sales rose 5.2% to $188.8 billion and it raised its full-year guidance again, as shoppers across income groups seek lower prices and its online, marketplace and advertising businesses grow fast. (Walmart, The Globe and Mail)

item.title: Japan's core inflation rises to 2.2% in October, its fastest this year, as energy subsidies end
item.description: Japan's core consumer prices rose 2.2% from a year earlier in October, up from 2.1%, as expiring energy subsidies lifted power and gas bills, keeping a December Bank of Japan rate hike in view. (Xinhua, MLQ.ai, ActionForex)

item.title: Canada seeks an interim tariff deal with the US by year-end, but says some sector tariffs will stay
item.description: Ottawa wants an interim deal by year-end to lower US tariffs on steel, aluminum, autos and lumber, but its trade minister says some tariffs will remain. (CBC News via Yahoo News Canada, Reuters via Free Malaysia Today)

item.title: The Labor Market Impact of Temporary High-Skill Immigration Programs
item.description: Temporary high-skill visa programs such as H-1B cut earnings of native science and engineering graduates by about 3.3%, but raised average US wages by about 1.3%, Borjas estimates. (George J. Borjas · Harvard Kennedy School)

item.title: Microsoft launches MAI Code 2 and Code 2 Flash, in-house coding models that come close to OpenAI's and Anthropic's at a lower cost
item.description: At Ignite, Microsoft released MAI Code 2 and Code 2 Flash, coding models it says nearly match GPT-6.1 Sol and Claude Opus 5.5 on four coding benchmarks at a fraction of the cost per task. (InfoWorld, The New Stack, Microsoft AI)

item.title: Anthropic's Claude agents settle two open problems in black-hole physics, with one result checked in the Lean proof assistant
item.description: Anthropic says Claude Fable 5.2 agents, working for about six weeks, solved two open quantum-gravity problems: a holographic phase transition and a proven bound on the lightest black holes. (Anthropic)

item.title: Jeveration: System One Models Now Generate
item.description: Jeveration turns a frozen vision-language model into an image generator that outputs a whole 512-pixel image in one forward pass, taking 78 ms, by conditioning all positions on a shared random state. (Yuhe Liu, Qi Li, Shihua Zhang et al. · National University of Singapore)

item.title: Weight-Space Programming Doesn't Need Transformers
item.description: When frontier LLMs write a model's weights by hand instead of training it, they abandon Transformers for sparse fact tables, which beat the Transformers they write with about 1,800 times fewer parameters. (Hyunjong Ok, Jaeho Lee · Pohang University of Science and Technology (POSTECH))

item.title: Ambient LLMs: Data-Efficient Supervised Fine-tuning via Temperature Matching
item.description: Ambient SFT adds one loss term to fine-tuning, matching the model's high-temperature predictions to those of its frozen pre-trained self, and beats standard SFT on small instruction, domain and reasoning datasets. (Giannis Daras, Marios Papachristou, Adam Klivans et al. · MIT, Arizona State University, University of Texas at Austin)

item.title: Depth Pro 2: Sharp and Temporally Consistent Metric Monocular Depth
item.description: Apple's Depth Pro 2 estimates metric depth from images and video at full resolution, ending the usual trade-off between sharp object edges and depth that stays stable from frame to frame. (Peiyun Hu, Marko Mihajlovic, Lyndon Duong et al. · Apple)

item.title: ALOHA Lightning: Learning Fast and Precise Manipulation
item.description: ALOHA Lightning lets operators physically guide a two-armed robot at near-human speed, then trains policies that fold shorts or insert batteries about as fast as people, from 50 demonstrations per task. (John Hua Yao. Qi Wu, Yihuai Gao, Chelsea Finn et al. · Stanford University)

item.title: Chase, Visa and Mastercard confirm breaches at outside vendors after an extortion gang leaks customer data
item.description: JPMorgan Chase, Visa and Mastercard say vendors were breached, exposing customer names and email addresses but no card numbers, after the N0n extortion group posted their data online. (The Register, SecurityWeek)

item.title: Broadcom patches a vCenter flaw that suspected Chinese state hackers exploited since September
item.description: Broadcom issued an emergency fix for a 9.8-rated vCenter Server authentication bypass that Mandiant says a suspected Chinese espionage group used as a zero-day to take over virtualized environments. (BleepingComputer, The Register)

item.title: The European Commission confirms a cyberattack in which hackers used a public AI hacking tool
item.description: The European Commission says attackers using a publicly available AI tool disrupted staff payroll, leave and medical reimbursement systems for more than ten days, with no evidence so far of a broad data breach. (The Register, The Record)

item.title: Congress publishes Nvidia and AMD's China chip licences, showing 879,000 AI chips approved
item.description: House committee chair Brian Mast released licence records showing US regulators approved more than 879,000 of 3.4 million requested Nvidia and AMD AI chips for China, including sales to Alibaba and Tencent. (House Foreign Affairs Committee, The Register)

item.title: YUL: Bringing Software Supply Chain Security to Coding Agents
item.description: YUL checks every software dependency a coding agent declares against the package registry and blocks stale or nonexistent versions, so agents end on the latest release in over 90% of affected runs. (Aman Sharma, Frank Reyes, Martin Monperrus · KTH Royal Institute of Technology)

item.title: FDA approves venglustat, the first treatment for the neurological symptoms of type 3 Gaucher disease
item.description: The FDA approved Sanofi's Infilbray (venglustat), a daily pill that reaches the brain, after a 43-patient randomized trial showed better neurological scores than standard enzyme infusions at one year. (FDA)

item.title: An off-the-shelf leukemia vaccine extends survival by nine months in a phase 3 trial, its developers report
item.description: In the 126-patient REGAL trial, people with acute myeloid leukemia in second remission who got the WT1 peptide vaccine galinpepimut-S lived a median 24.0 months, against 14.7 months on other treatments. (Memorial Sloan Kettering, BioPharm International)

item.title: Biogen's tau-lowering drug diranersen shows larger effects at two years in early Alzheimer's, in an open-label extension
item.description: Biogen says the twice-yearly 60 mg dose of diranersen slowed decline on the CDR-SB dementia scale by 38% at two years, up from 26% at 18 months, though the comparison comes from an open-label extension. (Biogen (GlobeNewswire), ReachMD)

item.title: Rainforest adaptation in late Homo erectus from southern China
item.description: Eight Homo erectus teeth from two caves in southern China, dated 324,000 to 184,000 years ago, carry chemical signs of a dense rainforest diet and of long journeys in childhood. (K. E. Westaway, R. Joannes-Boyau, W. Liao et al. · Macquarie University, Southern Cross University, Chinese Academy of Sciences Institute of Vertebrate Palaeontology and Palaeoanthropology)

item.title: Closest relatives of poxviruses prevail in human and animal guts worldwide
item.description: Mining 85,123 genetic datasets, researchers found egoviruses, the closest known relatives of poxviruses, in the guts of humans and livestock worldwide, hinting that the smallpox family began in animal guts. (Morgan Gaïa, Ulysse Guyet, Hans-Joachim Ruscheweyh et al. · French National Centre for Scientific Research (CNRS))

item.title: Nicotinamide Riboside for Patients With Early-Stage Parkinson Disease: The NOPARK Randomized Clinical Trial
item.description: In a 410-person Norwegian trial, a year of the NAD-boosting supplement nicotinamide riboside did not help early Parkinson's disease; symptom scores were slightly worse than with placebo. (NOPARK trial investigators (study director: Charalampos Tzoulis) · Haukeland University Hospital, University of Bergen)

item.title: Astronomers watch a Sun-like star spiral into a supergiant in Andromeda, with Webb confirming the merger
item.description: A star of about 0.7 solar masses merged with a supergiant seven times the Sun's mass in Andromeda after only seven orbits, and Webb observed the aftermath 47 days after the outburst peaked. (NASA, Phys.org)

item.title: Fiji declares a national disaster and Tonga a state of emergency as El Niño drought deepens
item.description: Fiji's cabinet declared a nationwide natural disaster and Tonga a 27-day state of emergency as El Niño-driven drought cuts water supplies, with effects expected to last until at least mid-2027. (Phys.org (AFP), RNZ, NZ Herald)

item.title: Observation of tunable superradiant frequency combs
item.description: Billions of ytterbium ions in a crystal synchronise through a shared microwave field and emit regular pulses at microwave and optical frequencies at once, forming a new kind of frequency comb. (Tian Xie, Rikuto Fukumori, Wai-Keong Mok et al. · California Institute of Technology; Stanford University)

item.title: Unblockable communication with gravity
item.description: Physicists sent the word "Gravity" through a brick wall by moving a 1.8-tonne elevator counterweight and reading its pull with a gravimeter, at one bit per minute. (Andrew J. Groszek, Charles W. Woffinden, Michael D. Harvey et al. · University of Queensland)

item.title: Fed minutes show almost all officials expect further rate hikes, and a couple raised the idea of a half-point move
item.description: Minutes of the Fed's October 27-28 meeting show officials held rates at 3.75-4% but almost all expect more hikes, setting up a December debate over how fast to tighten. (Federal Reserve, Federal Reserve (minutes), The Globe and Mail)

item.title: Lowe's raises its full-year sales forecast to about $92.5 billion as online sales jump 17.4%
item.description: Lowe's comparable sales rose 1.8% last quarter and it now expects full-year sales of about $92.5 billion, though it trimmed its margin forecast as costs rise. (Lowe's, Hardware Retailing)

item.title: Palo Alto Networks raises its revenue forecast after 39% growth and agrees to buy Applied Compute for $4.5 billion in stock
item.description: The cybersecurity company now expects fiscal 2027 revenue of up to $14.57 billion and is buying an AI model-training startup founded only last year. (Proactive Investors, MLQ.ai)

item.title: Alibaba's cloud revenue grows 53% as AI demand accelerates, but heavy spending keeps free cash flow negative
item.description: Alibaba's group revenue rose 10% to about $40.5 billion, its AI cloud unit grew 53%, and free cash flow was an outflow of $5.1 billion as data-centre spending climbed. (Alibaba Group (Business Wire via Yahoo Finance), Grafa, Crypto Briefing)

item.title: Irregular Demand: The Anti-Compromise Effect in the Field
item.description: In a Lyft experiment with 7.2 million riders, adding an expensive premium ride pushed customers toward the cheapest option and toward not riding at all. (Nicola Gennaioli, John A. List, Matthias Rodemeier et al. · Bocconi University; University of Chicago; Australian National University; Washington University in St. Louis)

item.title: Google launches Gemini 4 Neon, a fast frontier model priced at $3 per million input tokens
item.description: Google released Gemini 4 Neon, which ranks third on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index and first on its Coding Agent Index, at $3/$15 per million input/output tokens with a 1-million-token context. (Google)

item.title: Anthropic prices its IPO at $83 a share, raising $81.3 billion in the largest offering on record
item.description: Anthropic sold 980 million shares at $83, above its $70 to $78 range, raising $81.3 billion and valuing the Claude maker at about $1.5 trillion before Nasdaq trading under the ticker ANT. (TechCrunch, WIRED)

item.title: Counterfactual World Models: JEPAs That Reason About "What If"
item.description: Factual world models cannot answer "what if I had acted differently?" on their own, but for force-like disturbances adding the observed residual to the model's predicted action difference gives near-optimal counterfactuals with no retraining. (Randall Balestriero, Yann LeCun, Kerda Varaku · Brown University, New York University, AMI Labs)

item.title: Decoding Without a Decoder: Direct Pixel Prediction from Diffusion Transformers
item.description: Adding a linear pixel head to a fine-tuned diffusion transformer removes the latent decoder entirely, matching or improving quality, and the same separate head sets a new ImageNet FID record for pixel flow models. (Hansheng Chen, Shengqu Cai, Jan Ackermann et al. · Luma AI, California Institute of Technology, Stanford University)

item.title: Regularized Score Centering
item.description: Regularized Score Centering adds a reverse-KL penalty toward the data-generating policy to score-centered off-policy RL, stabilizing asynchronous LLM agent training and winning on all six agentic benchmarks tested. (Hao Bai, Chenlu Ye, Xuanchang Zhang et al. · UIUC, CMU)

item.title: $\pi^4$: A Foundation Model for 4D Scene Geometry and Motion
item.description: π⁴ is a 0.5B-parameter feed-forward model that recovers dense geometry, camera poses, metric scale, 2D/3D point tracks and moving-object masks from uncalibrated images or video in a single forward pass. (Yifan Wang, Weiguang Zhao, Ni Yang et al. · Shanghai Artificial Intelligence Laboratory, Shanghai Jiao Tong University, Zhejiang University)

item.title: Communicate the Change: Efficient Expert Parallelism via Activation Compression
item.description: EchoMoE retrofits existing mixture-of-experts models to send only a compressed change from an earlier layer's hidden state between GPUs, cutting inter-node traffic 58% and raising serving throughput 22.6%. (Fengyuan Liu, Jay Gala, Siva Reddy et al. · Mila - Quebec AI Institute, McGill University, Periodic Labs)

item.title: Attackers publish two credential-stealing versions of Microsoft's official Agent Framework package on PyPI
item.description: Two malicious releases of Microsoft's agent-framework Python package, downloaded about 200,000 times a month, stole cloud and developer credentials; developers who installed versions 1.26.1 or 1.26.2 should rebuild and rotate secrets. (BleepingComputer, The Register)

item.title: Intel signs its first outside customer for its 18A chip-making process, and Microsoft adopts its EMIB packaging
item.description: Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan says an unnamed company has signed on to make chips with Intel's 18A-P process, and that 18A yields have reached 70%, a step for Intel's effort to compete with TSMC. (Crypto Briefing, TrendForce)

item.title: Microsoft previews Windows Server 2028, which ships hardened by default with post-quantum key exchange
item.description: Windows Server 2028's public preview turns on hundreds of security settings from first boot, including Kerberos over NTLM and hybrid post-quantum TLS, and Microsoft warns that some older software may break. (BleepingComputer, Ars Technica)

item.title: A deployed four-city entanglement-based QKD network with real-time key delivery, benchmarked against finite-key security bounds
item.description: A Slovak quantum key distribution network links four cities over ordinary telecom fiber, runs all links at once and delivers finished keys to applications in real time, with honest post-processed key rates. (Gilberto Borges, Saeid Salari, Ekta Panwar et al. · Institute of Physics, Slovak Academy of Sciences)

item.title: FDA approves adrabetadex, the first drug shown to lengthen survival in infantile-onset Niemann-Pick disease type C
item.description: The FDA approved Lembaz (adrabetadex), a spinal injection given every two weeks, after treated patients with early-onset Niemann-Pick disease type C lived a median 8.5 years versus 4.9 years in matched controls. (FDA)

item.title: AriBio's oral Alzheimer's drug AR1001 slows decline in patients taking no other dementia drug, but not in its full phase 3 trial
item.description: In a 1,535-patient phase 3 trial, the daily pill AR1001 slowed decline by 31% among 604 patients on no other dementia drug, meeting a prespecified goal, but showed no significant effect overall. (MoneyToday, iNews24)
